name: macd_histogram_divergence_5s
author: adapted from quant_system
thesis: MACD histogram divergence (price makes new low but MACD histogram doesn't) signals momentum exhaustion before price reverses. Unlike RSI divergence, MACD histogram captures the rate of change of momentum, making it a leading indicator. The inefficiency exists because MACD divergence requires real-time pivot detection which most retail tools don't automate. Not fully arbitraged because divergence signals are subjective and hard to systematize.
mechanism: MACD divergence between price and momentum indicates that the dominant order flow is weakening. While price continues in one direction by inertia, the declining momentum shows fewer aggressive orders in that direction. Reversal occurs when the weakened flow is overwhelmed by opposing liquidity and new directional participants enter.

indicators.name: macd_hist
indicators.purpose: histogram — rate of change of momentum

indicators.name: price_pivot_low
indicators.formula: swing low with 5-bar lookback each side

indicators.name: hist_at_pivot
indicators.purpose: histogram value at price pivots for divergence

exit.signal_exit: exit on opposite MACD histogram cross

weaknesses: MACD on 1-min bars with 12/26/9 parameters is extremely lagging — by the time divergence confirms and histogram crosses zero, the reversal may be 70%+ done.
Profit factor of 1.08 is barely above breakeven. Slippage model errors would make this negative.
Divergence detection is inherently ambiguous — different pivot definitions produce different signals. Hard to validate out-of-sample.
prior_art: MACD histogram divergence. Alexander Elder's 'Trading for a Living'. Textbook setup.
adaptation_notes: Converted from 1min to 5s bars. Lookback multiplier: 12x. Adaptations: timeframe scaling to 5-second candles; apply to NIFTY/BANKNIFTY index instead of FnO universe; lookback period scaling for 5-second bars; stop/target recalibration for 5-second timeframe. Stop/target calibrated for options point-based exits. Universe narrowed to NIFTY index.
